question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away the supreme Kaula teaching?
premises: A person may possess wealth enough to fill an ocean with jewels.
Such wealth represents the greatest material abundance.
The verse raises this as a measure against giving the teaching.
inference: Even possession of immeasurable wealth is not a sufficient basis for transmitting the Kaula teaching.
uncertainties: The fused form ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is difficult and read as expressing the idea of making an ocean full of jewels.
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to make the ocean filled with jewels.
